The claimant has preferred this appeal challenging the judgment and award dated 23rd July, 2016 passed in MVC No.1443 of 2015 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raibag (for short,
hereinafter
referred to as the "Tribunal").
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to as per their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On February 18, 2015, Chidanand was traveling on his Bajaj M-80 two-wheeler with his wife and two children along Khanadal-Mugalkhod Road at a moderate speed.
When they reached the Garden land of Shankar Waddar, a driver of a Tata Sumo vehicle, coming from Mugalkhnd at high speed, drove recklessly and negligently.
The driver lost control of his vehicle, veering onto the wrong side of the road and collided with the two-wheeler carrying Chidanand and his family.
As a result, Chidanand sustained severe injuries to his face, head, and other parts of his body.
Immediately after the accident, Chidanand was taken to Dr. Nargund Hospital in Harugeri, where he received first-aid before being transferred to KLE NC: 2023:KHC-D:8909-DB Hospital in Belagavi.
He was admitted as an inpatient from 19th February, 2015 and unfortunately, he succumbed to his injuries on 26th February, 2015, at KLE Hospital in Belagavi.
Furthermore, it is stated that there has been a loss of dependency due to the deceased, and compensation is being sought.
3.1 In response to service of notice, respondents 1 and 2 have appeared and filed written statement.

The substance of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that the deceased- Chidanand was riding the two-wheeler with more than two persons, which is illegal and because of his negligence only accident occurred.

Respondent No.1 has admitted that he is the owner of Tata Sumo vehicle and driver of the said vehicle was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said Tata Sumo and the Insurance Policy was valid from 03rd September, 2014 to 02nd September, 2015 and hence, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.

4. The substance of the written statement of respondent No.2-Insurance Company is that, the deceased, on the date of NC: 2023:KHC-D:8909-DB accident, was riding an unregistered Bajaj M-80 two-wheeler that too carrying four persons in all, and this fact would clearly disclose that the Bharati @ Bharatavva W/O Chidanand ... vs Shankar S/O Neelkhant Satihal on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63650269/
3 rider of said two-wheeler has violated the terms, rules and conditions of Motor Vehicles Act.
Deceased ought to have carried only one pillion rider, which is permissible and further, he had no valid driving license to drive the motorcycle and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
The petitioners have not made the owner and insurer of the two-wheeler as party to the claim petition and hence the petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary parties.

Further it is stated that the deceased lost control over the motorcycle and dashed to Tata Sumo,
which shows the negligence on the part of the deceased himself who caused accident.
The complaint was lodged on 19th February, 2015 at 8.15 pm, after lapse of one day.
Panchanama drawn by police reveals that the road was straight and had sufficient width and the deceased himself has ridden two-wheeler on the wrong side and dashed to Tata Sumo.

The said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and the liability of the respondent No.2, if there is any, is subject to the validity and legality of the Registration Certificate, permit and driving license and also NC:
2023:KHC-D:8909-DB terms and conditions of the Policy, as per Motor Vehicles Act.
It is further contended that the driver of Tata Sumo was shown as accused after lapse of 24 days from the date of accident.
The petitioners, in collusion with Raibag Police, filed compliant and on all these grounds sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. Based on the rival pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal has framed the following issues for its consideration:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that the accident took place by rash and negligent driving of the driver of TATA Sumo bearing Registration No. KA-22/M-3754 i.e.
respondent No.1 on 18.2.2015 on Kahanadal- Mugalkhod Road, near garden land of Sahankar Waddar when the deceased Chidanand was riding the motorcycle M-80 along with the petitioners and he sustained head injury and died due to the said accident?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what extent and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
In order to substantiate their case, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW1 and two other witnesses were examined as PWs2 and 3 and produced 26 documents as Exhibits P1 to P26.
Respondents have not adduced on their behalf.

7. In the light of the above finding, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.9,01,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the claimants have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement in compensation.

8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant-claimants submits that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not awarding any amount towards love and affection of appellants 2 and 3 who have lost their father at their early age.
The Tribunal has also NC: 2023:KHC-D:8909-DB erred in awarding only Rs.8,16,000/- towards loss of dependency, which is contrary to the evidence on record.
He further submitted that Tribunal has committed an error in considering the notional income of the petitioner.
The Tribunal has also not awarded just and proper compensation on other heads.
On all these grounds, it is sought for enhancement in compensation.

9. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company sought to justify the impugned judgment and award and compensation awarded by the Tribunal and submitted that the same does not call for any interference in this appeal and hence, sought for dismissal of the appeal.

10. Having heard the arguments of both the learned counsel, the following points would arise for our consideration in this appeal:
(i) Whether the appellant/claimants have made out a ground for enhancement of compensation?
(ii) What order or award?

Our answer for the above points is as under:
Point No.1: partly in the affirmative; Point No.2: as per final order 12.
We have carefully examined the material on record.
The Tribunal has determined that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the Tata Sumo driver.
The respondents have not filed any appeal in this regard.
Exhibit P6-post-mortem report indicates that the deceased's age at the time of the accident was 35 years.

The Tribunal assessed the petitioner's income at Rs.
6,500/- per month, which does not align with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Following the guidelines, this Court has taken the notional income of the deceased to be Rs. 8,000/- per month for accidents of the year 2015.

13. In accordance with the Supreme Court's decision in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% should Bharati @ Bharatavva W/O Chidanand ... vs Shankar S/O Neelkhant Satihal on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63650269/
5 be added to the income for future prospects.

After this adjustment, the monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.8,400/-, resulting in a loss of dependency amounting to Rs.

14.

As per the rulings of the Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v.
PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157; and also in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. NANU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, since there are five claimants, each claimant is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.
